text: The star schema from T-SQL doesn't change at scale — a fact table surrounded by conformed dimensions is still the right default shape, from ten thousand rows to ten billion. What changes is what that fact table costs to scan, join, and update.
Before choosing star versus snowflake, fix the fact table's grain — the exact thing one row represents. Getting the grain wrong later is a redesign, not a tweak.
Snowflake schema normalizes a dimension to remove redundancy. At scale that trade-off sharpens: fewer duplicated bytes, but every query pays an extra join.
Slowly changing dimensions at scale become a targeted merge into a Delta table, the same MERGE INTO pattern from Databricks Lesson 22, not a full table rewrite.
Grain first, then schema, then the merge strategy that keeps it current. Next up: partitioning strategies — how that same fact table actually gets split up at scale.
